final_assessment: All 7 findings from the in-context proposal pass walked to resolution; zero stale, zero deferred, zero escalated, and every one took the obvious-fix lane — none involved a design choice or a scope call, which is the expected shape when a pass is auditing a prior walk rather than a proposal. Five of the seven were residue the earlier walk left at its own edges, and the post-fix completeness sweep found one more of exactly that kind that no review had reported: the recorded delta-size figures in the design size section went stale the moment finding 3 rewrote the spend-rendering rule. Those are now RECOMPUTED rather than hand-adjusted — 62,720 B, 153% of the R-crc-1 byte ceiling, 80% mandatory MODIFIED reproduction — and the same sweep cascaded a second Touchpoints annotation (instruction-loader.ts) that task 2.1 had outgrown. The substantive repair of the seven is finding 2: task 2.1 now carries the same AND EVERY CONSUMER phrase task 1.1 uses, and names both instruction-loader.ts sites, so the deletion cannot leave a projected field whose producer is gone. Nothing in this walk touched the change argument; all seven edits were to counts, task scope, predicted-touchpoint accuracy, and one rule split by surface.
